name: Córdoba
tagline: 50-year-old neighborhood joints, steaming locro, and the bife de chorizo that rules Nueva Córdoba.

La Ruleta de Pancho.description: A classic neighborhood joint with 50 years of history, a longtime favorite among locals.

Viejo Lobo.description: Voted "Córdoba's best traditional restaurant," classic Argentine cooking since 1997.

Alcorta Carnes y Vinos.description: A cosmopolitan steakhouse in Nueva Córdoba, famous for its bife de chorizo and wine list.

La Vieja Esquina.description: A criollo-food corner spot with more than 40 years of history: locro, humita, and acclaimed empanadas.

La Emilia.description: An upscale, relaxed steakhouse in the Ecodistrito de las Artes, with the city's best cuts.

Confitería La Oriental.description: A confectionery founded in 1863, the oldest in Córdoba's capital, located on the 9 de Julio pedestrian walk in the historic center.

Sorocabana.description: An emblematic café on San Jerónimo street facing Plaza San Martín, open since 1956 and a historic haunt for writers and journalists such as Daniel Salzano.

La City Bar.description: A corner bar on 25 de Mayo street next to the Iglesia de la Merced, a meeting point since 1970 for journalists, bank workers and downtown regulars.

Café de la Plaza.description: A neighborhood café in Alta Córdoba operating since 1930, declared a Site of Cultural Interest by the city council in 2017.

Marvic.description: An ice cream shop, bakery-café and restaurant facing Plaza Jerónimo del Barco in Alto Alberdi, a neighborhood classic with more than three decades of history.

Los Cubanitos.description: A neighborhood bakery-café open since 1953, known for its "cubanitos", the classic rolled pastry filled with dulce de leche.

Bron Café de Especialidad.description: A specialty coffee shop in the Güemes neighborhood, part of the new wave of Córdoba cafés focused on bean origin and roasting.

Mercado Norte.description: A municipal market inaugurated in 1928 in the city center, declared a Provincial Historic Monument in 1972; it houses butcher stalls, produce stands, regional sweets and quick eats.

El Ruedo.description: A steakhouse in the historic center with more than 50 years of history, an old-school classic on the corner of Obispo Trejo.

Los Cabritos.description: A family restaurant operating since 1976, specializing in roast kid goat from the Córdoba hills and homemade pastas.

Don Rogelio.description: A classic steakhouse in the Rogelio Martínez neighborhood marking 30 years in business, serving traditional cuts with neighborhood-style service.

La Casona de Alem.description: A classic steakhouse in the General Bustos neighborhood with more than two decades of grilled meats, set in a converted old house.

Argentum.description: A steakhouse in the Poeta Lugones neighborhood voted best parrilla in the city in 2018 and 2019, serving wood-fire grilled cuts, empanadas and locro.

IDA restaurant-bar.description: A restaurant-bar in Villa Belgrano offering a gourmet take on the grill, adding fish and salmon to the classic meat menu.

Matorral Parrilla.description: A steakhouse in Cerro de las Rosas focused on product traceability and premium cuts from selected cattle.

Ta Locro.description: A restaurant in the Pueyrredón neighborhood specializing in locro and other regional dishes, alongside grilled meats.

Lago Di Garda.description: An Italian restaurant in the city center operating since 1959, a historic reference point for Italian cooking in Córdoba.

Estación 27.description: A lomito (steak sandwich) and diner-food spot in the historic center, open since 1991 on 27 de Abril street.

Lomitos 348.description: A lomito shop in the Alberdi neighborhood founded in 1974, considered a must-try reference for the Córdoba-style steak sandwich.

Junior B.description: A Córdoba lomito chain born in 1999 in Nueva Córdoba, hugely popular with students for its generous portions.

Pierino.description: A neighborhood pizzeria open since 2002, known for its stone-baked, Córdoba-style pizzas.

Pizzería Don Luis.description: A downtown pizzeria founded in 1952, voted Córdoba's best pizzeria for 2024-2025.

Emir.description: A Middle Eastern restaurant in the Cofico neighborhood, a classic of Córdoba's Syrian-Lebanese community.

La Zete.description: A Middle Eastern restaurant born in 1992 on Obispo Salguero street, honored as a Gastronomic Legend of Córdoba.

El Celta.description: A seafood restaurant in the Alta Córdoba neighborhood, open since 2001.

República Restaurant.description: A chef-driven restaurant in Villa Belgrano led by chef Federico Ernst, offering 6- to 10-course tasting menus built around Córdoba hill-country produce, including oven-baked empanadas with chañar chutney.

El Club del Fernet.description: A bar in Nueva Córdoba devoted entirely to fernet, the city's signature drink, with personalized bottle labeling for regulars.

Hugo.description: A wine and cocktail bar in the Güemes neighborhood with 1970s-style decor, part of Córdoba's 2025 wave of new openings.

Archi Classic Bar.description: A classic-meets-modern cocktail bar in the Galería Barrio complex in Güemes, successor to the long-running gin bar La Gintonería.

Miski Mikuy.description: A Peruvian restaurant in the Alta Córdoba neighborhood, specializing in ceviche and coastal dishes.

Chulo.description: A Neapolitan pizza and street-food spot in the Alta Córdoba neighborhood, part of the city's newest wave of openings.

Casa Simona.description: A Spanish tapas restaurant in the Alta Córdoba neighborhood, with a cocktail list and dishes made for sharing.

Achalay!.description: A restaurant serving Salta-style, folk-inflected cooking in the General Paz neighborhood, with peña nights and dishes typical of northern Argentina.

Fanfarrón.description: A neighborhood bodegón in Güemes serving Argentine comfort-food classics in a casual bar setting.

Cherry Season.description: A specialty coffee and pastry shop in Nueva Córdoba, offering brunch and signature baked goods.
